svg.text: A recovery import builds everything in a staging area, checks it, then publishes a new share at once.
1 · operator on installation B
restore ns-photos from a backup alone,
stating that installation A is gone
2 · take the namespace's claim
claim owned at the next epoch; wait out A's
claim checks, so a partitioned A has stopped deleting
what it reads
the export; block headers in dfs-data;
keys objects at the bucket, every location
3 · staging area: no share serves it, no dedup lookup reads it
· check each location hint against the named block's header; find a stale chunk by listing the
namespace and reading headers; a chunk found nowhere fails the import
· key records: the union of the export's, the bucket's and every location's, over versions that authenticate
· re-derive the material census from the headers it resolved, not from the export
· recompute every count from the imported refs, and end with the audit
· import every other unexpired backup of the namespace it records as a detached, held snapshot
· write a backup record for every backup of the namespace found at a configured location
· rebuild each folder record's census and block count from that folder's mark set
· adopt the journals: record each, Restamp it, raise the tag counter above its tags,
before a tag is minted for any share
No block is copied: the refs name chunks still in dfs-data.
4 · one publish transaction
share photos-restored becomes
active with new FileIDs; the
staging identity is retired.
The namespace's GC pause record
is written: the namespace deletes,
relocates and collects nothing.
5 · operator's statement
every share of ns-photos is
recovered or given up: only then
is the pause record deleted and
GC starts
Interrupted, torn or refused before step 4
Nothing is served and nothing published. Its staging records are removed by its failure path or, if interrupted,
at the next start. An import is never resumed from a partial staging area: a new one starts over from the export.
